title: Primitive solvable permutation groups of prime degree: Galois's AGL(1,p) classification

problemStatement.formal: For prime $p$, define $\mathrm{AGL}(1, p) = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z} \rtimes (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times$ (semidirect product where units act multiplicatively on the additive group). Prove: (Forward) $\mathrm{AGL}(1, p)$ is solvable, acts faithfully and primitively on $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and has order $p(p-1)$. (Galois 1832) Every primitive solvable subgroup of $S_p$ embeds into $\mathrm{AGL}(1, p)$ (this direction may be split into a sub-OQ).
problemStatement.plain: Galois (1832) classified the primitive solvable permutation groups of prime degree p: they are exactly the affine groups AGL(1, p) of order p(p-1). The parent gallery proof proves S_n is solvable iff n ≤ 4 qualitatively; this open question asks for the quantitative refinement: for prime degree, the maximal solvable transitive subgroup of S_p is the affine group of order p(p-1), and the ratio p!/[p(p-1)] = (p-2)! measures the gap between solvability and full symmetric group.
whyMatters: Quantitative complement to the parent's qualitative threshold theorem: parent proves 'S_n solvable iff n ≤ 4'; OQ-06 sharpens this to 'for prime degree p, the largest solvable transitive subgroup of S_p has order p(p-1)'.

First formalization of the affine group AGL(1, p) as a Lean-verified primitive solvable permutation group. Mathlib has SemidirectProduct and IsSolvable but no AGL definition or primitive-permutation-group structure theorem for prime degree.

Frobenius-group prototype: AGL(1, p) is the canonical Frobenius group with abelian Frobenius kernel ℤ/pℤ and Frobenius complement (ℤ/pℤ)ˣ. The Lean formalization provides the foundation for any future Frobenius-group infrastructure in Mathlib.

Algebraic number theory connection: AGL(1, p) appears as the Galois group of splitting fields of irreducible degree-p polynomials whose factorization over the splitting field is a product of a p-cycle and a (p-1)-cycle. Formalizing AGL(1, p) is a prerequisite for connecting the parent's Galois-theoretic results to concrete number-theoretic examples.

proven: Classical mathematical result (Galois 1832, published 1846; modern reference: Rotman 1995 Theorem 9.11). Standard in every group theory textbook.

Mathlib has SemidirectProduct (Mathlib.GroupTheory.SemidirectProduct), IsSolvable (Mathlib.GroupTheory.Solvable), MulAction.IsPrimitive (Mathlib.GroupTheory.GroupAction.Primitive; verify at v4.26.0), Sylow theory (Mathlib.GroupTheory.Sylow), but no AGL definition and no primitive-permutation-group structure theorem.

insights: The full problem has two complementary directions: the forward direction (define AGL, prove it has the right properties — feasible in 3-4 sessions) and the Galois direction (every primitive solvable subgroup of S_p embeds into AGL — requires the structure theorem for transitive permutation groups of prime degree, which is not in Mathlib at v4.26.0 and may warrant a sub-OQ slug split).

AGL(1, p) is the canonical Frobenius group with abelian kernel. If Mathlib has a FrobeniusGroup typeclass at v4.26.0, the OQ-06 work can hook into it; if not, the OQ-06 work is independent and can leave a Frobenius-group instance as a follow-up.

The forward direction is similar in scope to OQ-04 (Jordan-Hölder instantiation): formalize a known group-theoretic structure using Mathlib's typeclass infrastructure, complete with 0 axioms and 0 sorries. The Galois direction is similar in scope to OQ-07 (Burnside): requires non-trivial group theory not in Mathlib, currently in-progress at 22 sessions with 1 axiom + 1 sorry.

Sharp 2-transitivity of AGL(1, p) on ZMod p (the affine action is faithful and 2-transitive, with stabilizer of two points trivial) gives primitivity automatically. Mathlib's `MulAction` API should support this reduction, though the exact lemma name needs to be verified at v4.26.0.

Connection to parent: parent's `Equiv.Perm.sign : Perm α →* ℤˣ` short-exact-sequence pattern (used for S₃, S₄) generalizes to AGL(1, p) — the determinant homomorphism (ZMod p)ˣ → ℤˣ / squares gives the parity layer.

compHom_smul_def (Hom.lean:59) + Equiv.Perm.smul_def (End.lean:90) provide a two-step rfl chain converting (g : AGL1Z p) • (x : ZMod p) into (AGL1Z.toPerm p g) x, which then reduces by AGL1Z.toPerm/toPermEquiv unfolding to g.trans + (g.scale : ZMod p) * x. Letting `show` perform the reduction at g = ⟨x, 1⟩ closes pretransitivity in one `simp` line.

isPretransitive_compHom (Hom.lean:67) is NOT applicable for AGL1Z because AGL1Z.toPerm p is not surjective for p ≥ 5 (|AGL(1,p)| = p(p-1) < p! = |S_p|). The hand-proof via the translation witness is mandatory — confirmed by S4-α PREP §3.
knowledge.noveltyAssessment: Not a novel mathematical result. Galois proved this in 1832; Rotman, Robinson, Cameron, and Wielandt all cover it as a standard textbook theorem. The Lean contribution is the *first formalization* of AGL(1, p) as a primitive solvable permutation group, providing infrastructure that Mathlib currently lacks and that future formalization work (concrete Galois groups of degree-p polynomials, Frobenius group theory) will reuse.
